Defect

`GrantRecipient` (`crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs`) carries the recipient's two keys as independent fields:

```rust
pub struct GrantRecipient<'a> {
    pub identity_pk: EcdsaVerifier,
    pub enc_pub: &'a X25519Public,
    pub display_name: String,
}
```

Since #954 these keys have **separate roles**: `identity_pk` is the mailbox routing address and the grant-ledger entry, while `enc_pub` is the HPKE target for both the grant blob and the sealed share pointer. Nothing structurally ties them together.

The binding exists — `import_contact` (`crates/engine/src/grants/contact.rs`) fail-closed-verifies the identity key's signature over the encryption subkey carried in the contact code — but `GrantRecipient` only *documents* that its `identity_pk` should come from a `Contact`. It does not enforce it.

## Why it matters

A future caller that takes `identity_pk` from the recipient's account and `enc_pub` from an unverified lookup seals the grant blob — which conveys the **read scope seed** — to an attacker-controlled X25519 key, while the share pointer routes to the honest recipient's inbox. The honest recipient cannot open it, so the mis-delivery is silent. That is a key-substitution attack the contact-code binding signature exists to prevent, and it became reachable the moment the two keys took different roles.

There is no production `GrantRecipient` producer today (only tests and the contract suite), which is why this is a hardening task rather than a live bug.

## Fix direction

Carry the bound pair as one value so the verified import is the only way in:

```rust
pub struct GrantRecipient<'a> {
    pub contact: &'a Contact,
    pub display_name: String,
}
```

`Contact` already exposes `identity_pk()`; it needs the encryption subkey exposed the same way if it does not already.

## Blocker to doing it in #954

The contract suite's live-API leg (`a_read_grant_delivers_its_share_pointer_through_the_live_mailbox`) mints its recipient through test-login, so the recipient's identity **scalar** lives server-side and the suite never holds it. Without that scalar the suite cannot produce a valid contact-code binding signature, so it cannot construct a `Contact` — taking `&Contact` today would cost the very real-caller-path test #954 added.

Resolving that is part of the work: either the suite gains a way to drive a recipient whose identity key it controls end to end, or the grant path accepts a verified-pair type that a test can construct without a full contact code.

Found by the `/crypto-privacy-review` gate on #954 (PR #961) and deliberately deferred there.

## Depends on

- Depends on #954 — this builds directly on the `EcdsaVerifier` field type that PR landed.
- Belongs with the grant and mailbox pipeline work in #635; land it alongside the first production `GrantRecipient` caller.

## Why

An earlier pass recorded dependencies as prose `## Depends on` / `## Blocks` sections. That is error-prone: the two directions are hand-maintained separately, so the reverse edge rots. An audit found forward edges present on 17 issues while **zero of seven** upstreams reciprocated. The native feature writes both directions from one call and cannot drift.

## The API — verified working on this repo

```bash

ID=$(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<M> --jq '.id')
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X POST \
  repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<N>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=$ID

```

One edge is already created as a test: **962 blocked_by 954**. Leave it and do not duplicate it.

## Scope

938, 939, 940, 942, 947, 948, 949, 953, 954, 956, 958, 959, 962, 963, 964, 965, 966

Simplify is back with a big set. I verified the two highest-consequence claims myself — both hold.

**The one that actually matters: the zeroization watchdog can pass vacuously.** `content_wipe.rs:40` only inspects deallocations where `layout.size() == SEALED_LEN`:

```rust
if layout.size() == SEALED_LEN && WATCHING.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
    // scan for MARKER, set LEAKED
}
```

If no allocation of exactly that size is freed during the window, nothing is ever scanned, `LEAKED` stays false, and `assert!(!LEAKED)` passes having tested nothing. It works today only because `chacha20poly1305::decrypt` happens to do `ciphertext.to_vec()` and truncate in place without reallocating — a third-party implementation detail, not a contract. There's no positive control. Given that a zeroization mistake in this repo previously broke 48 of 89 E2E tests, a security test that can silently stop testing is the finding I'd fix first: add an `INSPECTED` counter and assert it's non-zero.

**The largest structural win: `read_content` is now a strict special case of `read_content_range`.** Confirmed — the `project_child_version` + `Event::SnapshotUpdated` block is duplicated near-verbatim at `facade.rs:2398` and `2434`, and `read_content_inner` is a single-caller wrapper returning an anonymous `(Vec<u8>, u64, u64, u64)` that its only caller immediately re-splits. Collapsing removes ~50 lines, one public API item, and one of two projection sites.

## Findings

### [MEDIUM] The Service Worker does not enforce the security headers its own threat model depends on — it trusts the port

**CONFIRMED.** `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:296-315` (`sealed`), with `asResponse` at `pipe.ts:322-360`.

```ts
function sealed(status, headers = [], body = null): Response {
  const merged = new Headers();
  for (const [name, value] of headers) { try { merged.append(name, value); } catch { continue; } }
  merged.set('cache-control', 'no-store');
  return new Response(body, { status, headers: merged });
}
```

`pipe.ts` states its own rule twice — *"A same-origin port is still untrusted input"* and *"Vault plaintext must never reach a cache, whatever headers the tab sent"* — and then validates only **shape**. `content-type`, `x-content-type-options` and the `content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` sandbox all originate tab-side in `packages/client/src/media/range.ts:23-45` (`safeMimeType` + `hardening`). The SW re-emits whatever pairs arrive and forces only `cache-control`.

Concrete scenario: `/stream/<ticket>` is a **top-level-navigable same-origin URL**. The comment at `range.ts:19-22` correctly identifies that a shared file's attacker-chosen MIME type would otherwise execute as the app itself. But the enforcement lives on the wrong side of the boundary the code declares untrusted. Any regression in `range.ts`, or a port offered by a same-origin script (see LOW-2), yields `content-type: text/html` with no CSP at `https://app/stream/x` — attacker-controlled markup in the app origin, with the app's cookies and IndexedDB (`cipherbox-floors`, `cipherbox-snapshot-cache`, `cipherbox-staging`).

Exploitation today requires script execution on the origin, so this is defense-in-depth, not a live bug — but the cost of closing it is three lines, and the invariant is stated in the file that fails to enforce it.

**Fix** — force the hardening at the point the `Response` is constructed, exactly as `cache-control` already is, and clamp the type rather than trusting it:

```ts
merged.set('cache-control', 'no-store');
if (body !== null) {
  merged.set('content-type', safeMimeType(merged.get('content-type') ?? ''));
  merged.set('x-content-type-options', 'nosniff');
  merged.set('content-security-policy', "default-src 'none'; sandbox");
}
```

Export `safeMimeType` from `range.ts` (it is currently module-private). `range.ts`'s copy then becomes belt-and-braces rather than the sole guard.

### [MEDIUM] Assembled plaintext is stranded unwiped on every trust-violation exit of `open_content_range`, and `content_wipe.rs` structurally cannot see it

**CONFIRMED** (static; the residue path is unreachable by the new watchdog by construction).

`crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:244` and the two `Err` returns at `:260-265` and `:272-277`.

```rust
let mut plaintext = Vec::with_capacity(prealloc);   // :244  plain Vec, not Zeroizing
for index in leaves {
    let chunk = Zeroizing::new(open_chunk(...)?);   // :253  leaf IS wiped
    ...
    if chunk.len() as u64 != expected {
        return Err(OpenError::Trust(...));          // :261  `plaintext` drops UNWIPED
    }
    plaintext.extend_from_slice(&chunk[from..to]);
}
if plaintext.len() as u64 != length {
    return Err(OpenError::Trust(...));              // :273  same
}
```

The diff correctly makes each leaf a terminal-owner `Zeroizing` (`:251-256` — and I verified the mechanics: `aead::decrypt` allocates a `Vec` of capacity `chunk+tag` and truncates in place, so the freed block genuinely carries the plaintext, and `Zeroize for Vec<u8>` wipes the full capacity). But the **assembly buffer** — which by the time of a mid-range reject holds every already-verified leaf's plaintext — is a bare `Vec` and is freed unwiped on both fail-closed paths. A hostile or corrupt manifest is exactly the case where an attacker wants residue left behind.

Second half: `crates/engine/tests/content_wipe.rs:34-36,50` gates the watchdog on `layout.size() == SEALED_LEN` (32). The assembly `Vec` in that test has `prealloc == length == 4`, so its deallocation is invisible to the allocator hook. The test's module doc claims *"A ranged read must not strand a leaf's plaintext in freed memory"* — true for the leaf, and the test does prove that (I ran it: `1 passed`) — but a reader will take the guarantee as broader than it is.

Related, pre-existing but now newly load-bearing: for `open_content` (full file) `prealloc = min(size, MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES)`, so any file over that budget **reallocs repeatedly**, each growth orphaning an unwiped plaintext copy in the allocator. The ranged path happens to be exact (`prealloc == length`) so it does not grow — which is why the watchdog passes.

**Fix:**

```rust
let mut plaintext = Zeroizing::new(Vec::with_capacity(prealloc));
// ... unchanged body ...
Ok(core::mem::take(&mut *plaintext))   // moves the buffer out; the empty Vec's drop is a no-op
```

`mem::take` keeps the caller as terminal owner (AGENTS.md rule 7 — no callee wiping a caller-owned buffer) while every early `Err` now wipes.

And widen the watchdog so the guarantee is actually tested: drop the `layout.size() == SEALED_LEN` filter to `layout.size() >= MARKER.len()`, add a case that trips the `leaf {index} unsealed to …` reject after leaf 0 has already been appended, and assert no residue.

### [MEDIUM] Newest-port fallback answers a ticket from the wrong tab's registry, and a 404 is not retried

**CONFIRMED.** `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:227-236` (`portFor`), `:210-225` (`acquirePort`), `:118-131` (`respond`).

```ts
private portFor(clientId: string): MessagePortLike | null {
  const own = this.ports.get(clientId);
  if (own) return own.port;
  let newest: PortEntry | undefined;
  for (const entry of this.ports.values()) newest = entry;   // any other client's port
  return newest?.port ?? null;
}
```

`acquirePort` short-circuits on any non-null `portFor`, so it never asks the owning client for a port when *some other* client has one. The retry loop at `:118` retries only when `head === null` (timeout) — a `head.ok === false` 404 returns immediately.

Concrete scenario, no attacker: tabs A and B are open. The SW is killed (routine — Chrome stops idle workers in ~30s; the diff's own spec exercises exactly this via `ServiceWorker.stopAllWorkers`). Both tabs get `needPort`; B answers first. A's `<video>` issues its next range request. `portFor('A')` finds no entry for A, falls back to B's port, B's `StreamRegistry` has never seen A's ticket → `sealed(404)`. The media element sees a hard 404 mid-playback and stops. The two-tab spec at `media.spec.ts:180-201` only covers the case where *both* tabs already hold ports, so it does not reach this.

Security framing: not a confidentiality leak — a ticket resolving in the wrong registry is a miss, and registries are per-tab. But it is an availability failure on the plaintext read path arising from a deliberate cross-client fallback, and the fallback is also the enabler for LOW-2.

**Fix:** when the request carries a real `clientId`, do not fall back to another client's port — broker to the owner:

```ts
private portFor(clientId: string): MessagePortLike | null {
  const own = this.ports.get(clientId);
  if (own) return own.port;
  if (clientId !== ANONYMOUS_CLIENT) return null;   // ask the owner instead
  let newest: PortEntry | undefined;
  for (const entry of this.ports.values()) newest = entry;
  return newest?.port ?? null;
}
```

Keep the newest-port fallback only for `ANONYMOUS_CLIENT` (top-level navigation to a ticket URL, where the browser reports no client id). If you additionally want a 404 to be recoverable, treat `status === 404` on the first of the two attempts as a re-broker trigger.

### [MEDIUM] Follower media playback pushes every plaintext window onto the origin-wide BroadcastChannel

**CONFIRMED reachable.** `packages/client/src/leaderRelay.ts:193`, `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:108-111`, `packages/client/src/broadcast.ts:39`.

```ts
case 'downloadRange':
  return new Blob([await this.transport.downloadRange(read.node, read.offset, read.length)]);
```

`serveRead` (`leaderRelay.ts:170-177`) replies via `this.post(...)` on the `BroadcastChannel` named `cipherbox-engine` — a **broadcast**, delivered to every same-origin context, with `clientId` used only as a receiver-side filter. The plaintext `Blob` therefore lands in every tab, iframe and worker on the origin, which then discard it.

Reachability chain, verified end to end: `EngineProvider.tsx:57` → `createMediaService(client)` → `MediaService` constructor → `new MediaBroker(registry, config.reader)` where `reader` is the `EngineClient`; `EngineClient.downloadRange` (`engineClient.ts:163`) delegates to `this.current`, which is a `BroadcastTransport` whenever the tab is a follower. The diff's own `media.spec.ts:225-251` ("a follower tab routes its media read through the leader engine") asserts this path works.

This pattern is inherited from `download` and is not introduced here — but the amplification is qualitative, not quantitative. `download` fires once per user-initiated file open; `downloadRange` fires once per 1 MiB window for the entire duration of every media playback in every follower tab. A rare, bounded exposure becomes a continuous firehose of vault plaintext across an unauthenticated origin-wide bus.

Given #948/#949 are already filed as deferred siblings, I would file this as a follow-up rather than block: **route follower read *results* over a dedicated `MessagePort` (or `MessageChannel` per client) instead of the shared `BroadcastChannel`.** The channel is the right place for election and control traffic; it is the wrong place for plaintext. Note also that `new Blob([...])` gives the UA license to spill to disk for large payloads — bounded to 1 MiB by `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` on this path, but unbounded on the `download` path.

**PLAUSIBLE, could not verify:** whether any real deployment ever has a non-app same-origin context (an OAuth callback document, an embedded frame). If the origin only ever hosts the app itself, the practical exposure is limited to app code.

### [LOW] `downloadRange` accepts fractional offsets and silently truncates them

**CONFIRMED.** `crates/wasm/src/host.rs:386-397`.

```rust
if !offset.is_finite() || offset < 0.0 || !length.is_finite() || length < 0.0 {
    return Err(JsError::new("downloadRange offset and length must be non-negative finite numbers").into());
}
... read_content_range(node, offset as u64, length as u64)
```

The comment directly above says *"A saturating float-to-int cast would silently read a different window"* — but the guard covers sign and finiteness only. `offset = 1.5` passes and `as u64` truncates to `1`: the caller asked for one window and got a different one, with no error. Likewise `offset = 1e300` is finite and non-negative, saturates to `u64::MAX`, and clamps to an empty read — that one fails closed, so it is benign.

Today's only caller is `MediaBroker`, whose offsets come from `range.ts:parseOffset` (`Number.isSafeInteger`-gated), so this is not reachable in-tree. It is a trust-boundary input validation gap on a public `wasm_bindgen` export.

**Fix:**

```rust
let valid = |v: f64| v.is_finite() && v >= 0.0 && v.fract() == 0.0 && v <= (u64::MAX as f64);
if !valid(offset) || !valid(length) { return Err(JsError::new(
    "downloadRange offset and length must be non-negative safe integers").into()); }
```

### [LOW] Any same-origin client can become the pipe's broker, including anonymously

**CONFIRMED.** `packages/client/src/sw/install.ts:129-134`.

```ts
scope.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
  if (data?.type !== MEDIA_PORT_OFFER) return;
  const port = event.ports[0];
  if (port) pipe.adoptPort(port, event.source?.id);
});
```

`event.source?.id` is `undefined` for any client the SW cannot identify, collapsing to `ANONYMOUS_CLIENT = ''`. Combined with `portFor`'s newest-wins fallback (MEDIUM-3), an offer made without a resolvable source becomes the answering broker for **every** client that has no port of its own — and the SW will then stream that broker's `chunk` bytes with that broker's `status`/`headers` at a same-origin `/stream/` URL (see MEDIUM-1 for why the headers matter).

This requires script execution on the origin, so it is not an independent vulnerability — it is the amplification step that turns an XSS into a persistent same-origin content-serving primitive that survives the injecting document. Fixing MEDIUM-3's `portFor` removes most of it; additionally consider ignoring an offer with no `event.source?.id`, since `adoptPort`'s only legitimate caller is a window client.

### [LOW] `StreamRegistry` has no cap and no TTL

**CONFIRMED.** `packages/client/src/media/registry.ts:25-35`.

Tickets live until an explicit `revoke(url)` or `dispose()`. There is no eviction, so a long-lived tab that previews many files accumulates unbounded live bearer capabilities to plaintext, each of which stays redeemable by any same-origin script for the lifetime of the tab. The registry itself holds only a 16-byte `NodeId` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:80` — opaque, not a CID, not a filename, not key material), so nothing sensitive is *retained*; what accumulates is reachability.

Mitigating and worth recording: no production UI calls `createStreamUrl` yet (only `test/browser/media.ts:121`), so this is latent. `EngineProvider.tsx:66` does dispose the service on logout via `rebuild`, which clears the registry — that part is correct.

**Fix:** cap the map (LRU-evict the oldest ticket past, say, 64) and/or expire a ticket some minutes after its last `lookup`.

## Areas I checked and found clean

State these plainly so they are not re-litigated:

- **No crypto or codec in TypeScript.** Grepped the full diff: `packages/client`, `apps/web` and the service worker contain no cipher, no hash, no CBOR/CID encoding. The single `crypto.*` call in shipped code is `globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()` for ticket minting (`registry.ts:22`), which is opaque-capability generation, not a crypto operation, and is injectable for determinism. `crypto.subtle.digest` appears only in the Playwright harness (`test/browser/media.ts:139`). AGENTS.md rule 4 holds.

- **No secret material in any persistent store.** No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `document.cookie` or `indexedDB` write anywhere in the diff. The only Cache writer is `precacheAppShell` (`precache.ts:44-50`), whose `CacheLike` interface deliberately exposes no `put` — vault data is *structurally* unable to reach the cache, not merely policed. `resolveEntry` (`precache.ts:141-152`) rejects cross-origin entries and explicitly rejects `STREAM_PATH_PREFIX`. `deleteStaleCaches`'s `cipherbox-` prefix touches CacheStorage only and does not collide with the `cipherbox-floors` / `cipherbox-snapshot-cache` / `cipherbox-staging` IndexedDB databases (separate namespace — verified).

- **No key, seed or plaintext crosses into the Service Worker.** The SW receives exactly: a random ticket string, a raw `Range` header, an already-resolved status/header set, and transferred plaintext windows it never inspects, caches or retains. The port is a private `MessageChannel`, not the `BroadcastChannel`.

- **Ticket opacity.** `/stream/<uuidv4>` encodes no CID, no `ipnsName`, no filename, no node id. `MediaService.createStreamUrl` (`service.ts:77-84`) hard-refuses to mint unless a Service Worker actually controls the tab, so a ticket cannot escape to the origin server via an unintercepted fetch. That guard is exactly right and I want to call it out.

- **Zeroization discipline at the WASM boundary.** `host.rs:377,405` wrap a *returned-by-value* `Vec<u8>` — the function is the terminal owner, no caller-owned buffer is touched. `engineHost.ts:38-42`'s `ownedBuffer` correctness claim holds: `Uint8Array::from(&[u8])` allocates in the JS heap and copies, so the returned view is never a window onto WASM linear memory, and there is no read of a WASM-backed buffer across a suspension point anywhere in the diff. No detached-view hazard.

- **Range arithmetic is memory-safe.** In `open_content_range`, `from <= to <= expected == chunk.len()` holds for all inputs (`saturating_sub` monotonicity), so `&chunk[from..to]` cannot panic; `offset + length <= manifest.size` post-clamp, so the `saturating_add` cannot wrap; `chunk_size == 0` is rejected at `decode_root` (`dag.rs:243`) *and* guarded fail-safe in `leaf_range_for_byte_range` (`read.rs:297`). The exhaustive `every_offset_and_length_matches_the_whole_file_slice` test (`mod.rs:~510`) is good coverage.

- **The new per-leaf framing check is a genuine fail-closed strengthening, not a weakening.** Ranged reads lose the end-to-end `plaintext.len() == manifest.size` proof; `mod.rs:258-265` replaces it with a per-leaf `chunk.len() == chunk_size.min(size - leaf_start)` reject, which proves byte alignment locally. A short middle leaf — which would silently shift every downstream byte — is a `Trust` violation. Correct design.

- **Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry (AGENTS.md rule 8) — satisfied.** I traced *both* producers, not just the one the test covers. `frame_and_seal` (`chunk.rs:88-97`) uses `slice::chunks`, so a short non-final leaf is unrepresentable. More importantly the **streaming** producer, `ContentWriter` (`write.rs:63-127`), is also safe: `max_pending = min(declared_size, chunk_size)` and `seal_pending` fires only at `pending.len() == chunk_size`, so every leaf sealed in `push` is exactly full and only `finish`'s tail can be short; `assemble` then cross-checks `leaf_cids.len() == expected_leaf_count(observed, chunk_size)` with a release-active `Err` (`dag.rs:174`). I walked the short-write case (`declared 100, pushed 20`) and the sub-chunk case (`declared 10`) — both produce manifests the new reader accepts. The new check is an `if … return Err`, not a `debug_assert!`. No release build can publish content its own reader rejects.

- **Capped fetch relocation.** `FetchHttp.sendCapped` (`seams/http.ts:58-107`) enforces the bound while draining `Response.body` — a real peak-memory bound, correctly replacing the post-buffer check the doc comment at `crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs:148` used to apologize for. `HttpAdapter::send_capped` (`seams_bridge.rs:600-616`) keeps a Rust-side backstop and fails closed on an unrecognized `kind`, which is the right default. `Number.isFinite` handling of a missing/garbage/negative `content-length` all degrade safely to the streaming path. `capped_count`'s `required_u64` → `unwrap_or_default()` on a missing field only affects a diagnostic count on an already-failing path.

- **Determinism seams.** No clock or RNG call added to `crates/core` or `crates/engine`. `setTimeout`/`randomUUID` appear only in browser-seam code (`packages/client`), which is where they belong, and both are injectable.

- **Metadata leakage.** The only vault-derived values crossing into the SW are plaintext `size` (as `content-length`) and MIME type — both same-origin, same-device, and both inherent to the HTTP semantics being emulated. Fix: `Zeroizing::new(Vec::with_capacity(prealloc))`, and return `Ok(core::mem::take(&mut *plaintext))` so the caller stays terminal owner (AGENTS.md rule 7 — a callee must never wipe a caller-owned buffer).

**1.3 [VERIFIED] The zeroize watchdog can pass vacuously — `crates/engine/tests/content_wipe.rs:36-53, 115-118`.**
Flagged independently by both the simplify and crypto gates. `dealloc` only inspects `layout.size() == SEALED_LEN`, so if no allocation of exactly that size is freed in the window, nothing is scanned and `assert!(!LEAKED)` passes having tested nothing. It works today only because `chacha20poly1305::decrypt` happens to `to_vec()` and truncate in place — a third-party detail. Fix: add `static INSPECTED: AtomicUsize`, bump it in `dealloc` alongside the scan, and assert `INSPECTED > 0` next to `!LEAKED`. Then widen the filter (e.g. `layout.size() >= MARKER.len()`) and add a case that trips the `leaf {index} unsealed to …` reject *after* leaf 0 has been appended, asserting no residue — that is the regression test for 1.2. Verify the new test actually fails if you revert 1.2; a test that cannot fail is worthless here.

**1.4 [VERIFIED] Newest-port fallback answers from the wrong tab's registry — `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts` `portFor`.**
Flagged by both crypto and security. `acquirePort` correctly targets the owning client, but `portFor` short-circuits first with a newest-wins fallback. Two tabs + a routine SW restart (the diff's own spec kills the worker) means tab A's ticket resolves against tab B's registry → hard 404 mid-playback, no retry. Fix: return `null` for a non-anonymous `clientId` with no own port so the owner gets asked; keep the newest-port fallback only for `ANONYMOUS_CLIENT`. Crypto rated this MEDIUM: `sealed()` forces only `cache-control` and re-emits tab-supplied `content-type` / `nosniff` / CSP, even though the file's own doc declares the port untrusted input. Security traced the same code and called it well done, because `safeMimeType` + `nosniff` + `default-src 'none'; sandbox` *are* present on every head today via `media/range.ts`. Both are factually right; they differ on whether enforcement belongs on the trusted side of the boundary.

**Adjudicate this yourself and say which way you went.** My lean is to apply it — it is ~3 lines, and a guard that lives only on the side the code calls untrusted is one refactor away from being absent. If you apply it: force `nosniff`, the sandbox CSP, and a `safeMimeType`-clamped `content-type` in `sealed()` when a body is present, exporting `safeMimeType` from `range.ts`; `range.ts`'s copy then becomes belt-and-braces. Add the test the crypto gate asked for: a port answering `open` with `[['content-type','text/html']]` and no CSP must still yield a hardened, clamped response.

**2.1 Collapse `read_content` into `read_content_range`** — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2388-2459`, `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:191-197`. `open_content_range` clamps `length` to `manifest.size` before the prealloc, so `read_content_range(node, 0, u64::MAX)` *is* the whole-file read with no over-allocation. **2.2 Drop `ok` from the head wire message** — `packages/client/src/media/protocol.ts:33-41`. Every producer sets it as exactly `status === 200 || status === 206`; the only consumer is `pipe.ts:126`; nothing cross-checks the two, so `ok:true, status:404` is representable. Found by the `/crypto-privacy-review` gate on #641 (PR #951) and deliberately deferred there — the pattern is inherited, not introduced, but that PR changes its cost by orders of magnitude.

## Defect

A follower tab's media reads return **vault plaintext over an origin-wide, unauthenticated bus**.

`packages/client/src/leaderRelay.ts:193`:

```ts
case 'downloadRange':
  return new Blob([await this.transport.downloadRange(read.node, read.offset, read.length)]);
```

`serveRead` replies via `this.post(...)` on the `BroadcastChannel` named `cipherbox-engine`. `BroadcastChannel` is a **broadcast**: every same-origin context — every other tab, iframe, and worker on the origin — receives the message and its plaintext payload, then discards it. `clientId` is only a receiver-side filter, not an access control.

Reachability, traced end to end: `EngineProvider.tsx:57` → `createMediaService(client)` → `MediaService` → `new MediaBroker(registry, config.reader)` where `reader` is the `EngineClient`; `EngineClient.downloadRange` (`engineClient.ts:163`) delegates to `this.current`, which is a `BroadcastTransport` whenever the tab is a follower. #951's own browser test `a follower tab routes its media read through the leader engine` asserts this path works.

## Why now, when `download` has always done this

The amplification is qualitative, not just quantitative:

- `download` fires **once per user-initiated file open** — a rare, bounded exposure.
- `downloadRange` fires **once per 1 MiB window, for the entire duration of every media playback, in every follower tab** — a continuous stream of vault plaintext across the bus.

A rare leak becomes a firehose.

Secondary: `new Blob([...])` gives the user agent license to spill large payloads to disk. Bounded to `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` (1 MiB) on the ranged path, but unbounded on the `download` path.

## Threat model, stated honestly

Exploiting this requires script execution on the origin, and such a script already has more direct routes — `LeaderRelay.receive` serves `cb:read` off the same channel with no sender check, and `WireRead.download` returns any node's full plaintext with no ticket. So this is **not a new privilege boundary**; it is defence-in-depth and blast-radius reduction. It matters because the channel is the wrong instrument: it is right for election and control traffic, and wrong for carrying plaintext.

Unverified: whether any real deployment ever hosts a non-app same-origin context (an OAuth callback document, an embedded frame). If the origin only ever serves the app, practical exposure is limited to app code.

## Fix direction

Carry follower read **results** over a dedicated `MessagePort` (or a per-client `MessageChannel`) established during election, and keep `BroadcastChannel` for election and control messages only. The leader already knows each follower's `clientId`, so a port handshake is a small addition to the existing relay.

## Scope

- Establish a per-follower `MessagePort` at leadership swap and tear it down on step-down.
- Route `cb:read` responses — `download`, `downloadRange`, `snapshot` — over the port; leave election and focus traffic on the channel.
- Transfer the buffer rather than copying it, as the SW pipe already does.
- Cover it: a second same-origin context must observe election traffic and **no** plaintext payload while a follower streams.

## Depends on

Recorded as a native dependency, not prose. #641 must land first — the `downloadRange` relay path this changes is introduced there.

## Defect

The app-shell cache is never rotated, so a user's offline shell pins whichever deploy they first installed.

- `packages/client/src/sw/precache.ts:12` — `APP_SHELL_CACHE` is a constant, so the cache name never changes.
- `packages/client/src/sw/precache.ts:75` — `deleteStaleCaches` explicitly excludes the live cache, so it cannot rotate it.
- `apps/web/vite.config.ts:54` — `entryFileNames: SW_FILE`, no build stamp.

`sw.js` contains no build-varying bytes: its content is a pure function of `packages/client/src/sw/**`. A deploy that changes only app chunks therefore leaves it byte-identical, the browser finds no worker update, `install` never re-fires, and `precacheAppShell` never re-runs. The offline navigation fallback (`precache.ts:114`) serves deploy-N's `index.html` indefinitely.

## A second-order effect compounds it

Production serves the SPA with `try_files {path} /index.html` (`docker/Caddyfile:18`) and the deploy wipes the web root (`rm: true`, `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml:460`). A redeploy landing mid-`install` makes `cache.addAll` (`precache.ts:52`) receive `200 text/html` for a now-missing hashed asset and cache the shell HTML under a `.js` URL. `resolveEntry` validates the URL, never the response.

## Scope of impact — stated precisely

**Online users self-heal.** `respondFromAppShell` handles navigations network-first (`precache.ts:111-112`), so a returning user gets the new `index.html`, whose new hashed asset URLs are not in `precached`, fail `appShellClaims` (`:91`), and pass through to the network.

The real impact is a stale offline shell plus unbounded cache growth across deploys. This is an integrity and correctness defect, not a live exploitation path. Recording that explicitly because an earlier draft of this finding overstated it as a permanent white-screen, which is wrong.

- Stamp a build id into the worker via `define` on the nested `build()` at `apps/web/vite.config.ts:43-58`, and key `APP_SHELL_CACHE` off it, so both the update check and the rotation follow the build.
- Optionally carve `/assets/*` out of the Caddy SPA fallback so a missing asset 404s and `addAll` rejects rather than caching HTML under a `.js` URL.

## Defect

Reading a file larger than `MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES` orphans an un-wiped copy of its plaintext in the allocator on **every** buffer growth.

`crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:218-219` on `main`:

```rust
let prealloc = manifest.size.min(limits::MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES as u64) as usize;
let mut plaintext = Vec::with_capacity(prealloc);
```

When `manifest.size` exceeds the budget, `prealloc` is capped below the final length, so the `extend_from_slice` loop reallocates repeatedly. Each growth copies the accumulated plaintext to a new allocation and frees the old one **without zeroizing it** — `Vec`'s realloc has no idea the bytes are secret. A single large read therefore leaves a geometric series of partial plaintext copies in freed heap.

## Not fixed by the Zeroizing change on #641

PR #951 wraps the buffer in `Zeroizing` (`content/mod.rs:235`), which fixes the *abandoned-on-error* case. It does not fix this one: `Zeroizing` wipes the buffer it currently owns at drop, and has no hook on reallocation, so every superseded allocation is already gone by then.

The ranged path is unaffected in practice — `prealloc` equals the exact window length there, so it never grows. This bites the whole-file read, where `length` is the full `manifest.size`.

## Not caught by the existing watchdog

`crates/engine/tests/content_wipe.rs`'s allocator watchdog inspects frees at leaf-ciphertext sizes. A growing assembly buffer frees at a geometric progression of much larger sizes, so the residue is invisible to it regardless of how the filter is tuned.

## Fix direction

Either reserve the true final length up front rather than capping at the record budget — the manifest already states `size`, and the cap protects against a hostile manifest rather than a legitimate large file, so the two concerns want separating — or assemble through a type that zeroizes on grow (a wrapper that wipes the old buffer before releasing it).

The cap exists so a hostile manifest cannot drive an unbounded allocation. That is a real concern and should stay, but it should be enforced as a *rejection* of an over-budget manifest rather than as a silent under-reservation that produces residue.

## Reachability

`MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES` bounds a resolved record, not a content file, so any file above it hits this on every full read. Distinct from #918 (op-queue plaintext) and #936/#956 (core codec scrub) — this is the engine content-assembly path.

Found by the `/crypto-privacy-review` gate on #641 (PR #951) and deferred there.

So #976 is genuinely new.

It also turned out to be **more than the "caveat" it was reported as.** Checking `main`:

```rust
let prealloc = manifest.size.min(limits::MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES as u64) as usize;
let mut plaintext = Vec::with_capacity(prealloc);
```

That cap is below the final length for any file bigger than the record budget, so the assembly loop reallocates repeatedly — and each growth frees the previous buffer, holding accumulated plaintext, without zeroizing. A single large read leaves a geometric series of partial plaintext copies in freed heap. `Zeroizing` can't help: it wipes the buffer it owns at drop, and the superseded allocations are long gone by then. The existing watchdog can't see it either, since it inspects leaf-ciphertext-sized frees and these are a progression of much larger ones. The issue notes the cap should stay but be enforced as a *rejection* of an over-budget manifest rather than a silent under-reservation.

## Problem

Both `send_capped` implementations check the cap only *after* the chunk has been materialized, so the real peak-memory bound is `max_bytes` plus one transport chunk — not `max_bytes`. The seam's own contract text says otherwise, in two different ways, and neither arm has a test that exercises the overshoot.

### The bound is cap + one chunk, on both arms

`packages/client/src/seams/http.ts` — `reader.read()` resolves `value` first, and only then:

```ts
if (total + value.byteLength > maxBytes) {
  await reader.cancel();
  return { kind: 'tooLarge', observed: total + value.byteLength, limit: maxBytes };
}
```

`crates/desktop-seams/src/http.rs` does the same shape with `response.chunk().await` and `body.len() + chunk.len() > max_bytes`.

Neither is a memory-safety hole: transport chunk sizes are bounded well below the 4 MiB content cap in practice, and both arms still abort the drain rather than buffering the whole body. It is a precision problem in a contract that other code reads as exact.

### The doc overclaims, and draws a distinction that does not exist

`Http::send_capped` in `crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs` currently distinguishes the two arms:

- desktop is described as "the true peak-memory bound at the content fetch boundary"
- WASM is described as draining the body under the cap and "never materializes an over-cap body"

Both claims are off by one chunk, and the two arms in fact behave identically here — the distinction the doc draws is not real. The text should state one bound for both: the drain aborts once the accumulated body would pass the cap, bounded by at most one chunk of overshoot.

### No test reaches the first-chunk-over-cap branch

Every oversize case in `packages/client/src/seams/http.test.ts` uses `producedBody(100, 100)` against a cap of 1000, so `total` is always non-zero when the cap trips and the branch where the *first* chunk alone exceeds the cap never runs. A case such as `producedBody(4096, 4)` against a cap of 1000, asserting `observed === 4096`, covers it. The desktop conformance suite wants the matching case.

## Gate

The `packages/client` vitest suite covers a single chunk larger than the cap; the `crates/desktop-seams` conformance suite covers the same shape. The `send_capped` doc states one bound for both arms and no longer claims an over-cap body is never materialized.

#641 — `sendCapped` and the doc text both land there.

Production serves the SPA with `try_files {path} /index.html` (`docker/Caddyfile:18`) and the deploy wipes the web root (`rm: true`, `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml:460`). A redeploy landing mid-`install` makes `cache.addAll` (`precache.ts:52`) receive `200 text/html` for a now-missing hashed asset and cache the shell HTML under a `.js` URL. `resolveEntry` validates the URL, never the response.

## Scope of impact — stated precisely

**Online users self-heal.** `respondFromAppShell` handles navigations network-first (`precache.ts:111-112`), so a returning user gets the new `index.html`, whose new hashed asset URLs are not in `precached`, fail `appShellClaims` (`:91`), and pass through to the network.

The real impact is a stale offline shell plus unbounded cache growth across deploys. This is an integrity and correctness defect, not a live exploitation path. Recording that explicitly because an earlier draft of this finding overstated it as a permanent white-screen, which is wrong.

## Fix direction

- Stamp a build id into the worker via `define` on the nested `build()` at `apps/web/vite.config.ts:43-58`, and key `APP_SHELL_CACHE` off it, so both the update check and the rotation follow the build.
- Optionally carve `/assets/*` out of the Caddy SPA fallback so a missing asset 404s and `addAll` rejects rather than caching HTML under a `.js` URL.

### What was built

Follower read results (`snapshot`, `siweChallenge`, `download`, `downloadRange`) no longer ride the origin-wide `cipherbox-engine` `BroadcastChannel`. The follower asks where this leadership takes ports (`cb:portWanted` → `cb:portHost`), dials it through the Service Worker, names itself (`cb:portHello`), and adopts the port once the leader greets with the active leadership token. Reads then flow `cb:portRead`/`cb:portResult` over that port, with `ArrayBuffer` results **transferred**, not wrapped in a `Blob`.

A `BroadcastChannel` carries no transferables, so a Service Worker is the only cross-tab route for a `MessagePort`. The worker is a stateless forwarder — it names a client back to itself and forwards the far end of a `MessageChannel`, reading neither.

Identified while building #972 and deliberately left out of that PR, which scoped itself to follower read **results**.

## The gap

#972 moves `snapshot`, `siweChallenge`, `download`, and `downloadRange` results off the origin-wide `cipherbox-engine` `BroadcastChannel` and onto a per-follower `MessagePort`. The write direction was not moved.

`pushChunk` still rides the channel as a `Blob` handle, so upload plaintext is delivered to every same-origin context — every other tab, iframe, and worker on the origin — which then discards it. Command arguments travel the same way: filenames, contact codes, and the `siweLogin` signature.

The asymmetry is now the notable part. After #972 a follower's reads are private to the leader and unreadable by a bystanding context, while its uploads are not. Anyone reasoning about the channel from the read path will draw the wrong conclusion about the write path.

## Threat model, stated honestly

Same as #972's: exploiting this requires script execution on the origin, and such a script already has more direct routes. This is defence-in-depth and blast-radius reduction, not a new privilege boundary. It matters because the channel is the wrong instrument for carrying plaintext, and #972 has already built the right one.

## Why it is cheap now

The port, its handshake, its adoption gate, and the transfer path all exist after #972. `pushChunk` becomes a transfer over the established port rather than a `Blob` on the bus — the expensive part of the work is already paid for.

## Scope

- Route `pushChunk` payloads over the per-follower `MessagePort`, transferring the buffer rather than wrapping it.
- Move value-bearing command arguments off the channel by the same route.
- Extend the existing coverage: the second same-origin context in `leadership.spec.ts` must observe **no** upload plaintext and no command arguments while a follower writes, exactly as it already asserts for reads.

This PR is about grant delivery addressing — it routes grant mailbox delivery to the recipient's ECDSA identity key rather than an encryption key, and draws the mailbox idempotency key from entropy.

An empty `pulls/N/reviews` array plus a "Review skipped — Draft detected" body is ambiguous: it looks identical whether the PR was never reviewed or was reviewed clean and then overwritten. I read the post-push state and wrongly concluded a sub-agent had fabricated its "no actionable comments" quote — it had read the genuine pre-push body, and its own rebase push destroyed the evidence.

READ-ONLY verification task for FSM1/cipher-box. **Do NOT push anything, do NOT modify any PR branch, do NOT change any PR's draft state.** Your job is purely to answer: would merging these PRs break `main`?

## Background — why this is being asked
PR #971 just merged to `main` (tip `6ab2a3c2a`). It added a **required** field `folderName: string` to a type in `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts`, and changed `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`, `packages/client/src/index.ts`, `packages/client/src/testkit.ts`, `packages/client/src/worker/engineWasm.ts`, and `packages/client/src/worker/commandCodec.ts`.

Four PRs today were reported `MERGEABLE` by GitHub with fully green CI and would still have broken `main`, because their checks ran against a stale base. `git merge-tree` reported no textual conflict in every one of those cases too — a required interface member added on main is invisible to conflict detection and only shows up as a type error. The most recent catch: #961 carried its own `unknown: Vec::new()` fixture that failed E0308 against #957's `PreservedFields` change.

So do not trust `mergeable: MERGEABLE`, do not trust green CI on the PR, and do not trust a clean `git merge-tree`. **Build the actual merge and compile it.** That is the only reliable test.

## What to check
Two PRs, in this order:

1. **#982** — branch `fix/972-follower-read-port`, 11 commits behind main. Shares `packages/client/src/index.ts`, `packages/client/src/testkit.ts`, `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.test.ts` with #971.

Shares six files with #971: `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, `packages/client/src/index.ts`, `packages/client/src/testkit.ts`, `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.test.ts`, `packages/client/src/worker/engineWasm.ts`, `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts`.

## Method
For each PR, in a SCRATCH worktree under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/d6d4959d-7e94-4b31-b5a4-2baeac1e123c/scratchpad/` (NOT in the main checkout at `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box`, and NOT in any `.claude/worktrees/` directory — those hold live branches other work depends on):

```
git worktree add --detach <scratch>/merge<PR> origin/main
cd <scratch>/merge<PR>
git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t merge --no-edit origin/<branch>
```

Then compile. Set a scratch-local `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per merge (e.g. `<scratch>/merge982/tgt`) — NEVER share one across worktrees, it silently reuses stale binaries and makes every branch report identical passing counts.

Run and capture VERBATIM exit codes and any errors:
- `pnpm install` (needed before any TS gate; each worktree needs its own `node_modules` — do NOT symlink from the main checkout)
- `pnpm -r --if-present run typecheck`  ← **this is the gate most likely to catch the `folderName` breakage**

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- `cargo fmt --all --check` (must be `--all`, never `-p`)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (`--workspace` never builds wasm32)

If a merge produces a textual conflict, STOP for that PR, record exactly which files and hunks conflicted, and move on to the other — do not attempt to resolve it.

If a gate fails, capture the FULL error (file:line, error code, expected-vs-found) — that is the most valuable part of your report.

Note: `crates/contract` tests silently SKIP when `CONTRACT_API_URL` is unset (binary finishes in 0.00s via `require_stack!`). Do not report those as passing. `packages/client/test/browser/*.spec.ts` is NOT covered by `pnpm -r run test` — vitest is scoped to `src/**/*.test.ts` there — so do not claim browser coverage from that gate.
